title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Applicable Persons
tiers.description: Directors, employees, advisers and consultants of LIN. Subject to the general Inside Information dealing prohibition; the general purpose statement says this tier should 'never engage in short term trading', though the substantive short-term trading rule (section 6) is expressed as applying only to key management personnel and their Related Persons.

tiers.name: key management personnel
tiers.description: Has the meaning in AASB 124: directors, the company secretary, persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling LIN's activities, and any other person notified by the Board from time to time. Subject to Closed Period/Prohibited Period trading bans, short-term trading ban, notification and pre-clearance requirements, the derivatives criteria in section 10, and the margin lending disclosure regime in section 9.

tiers.name: Related Persons
tiers.description: Spouses, de facto spouses, parents and children of Applicable Persons. Key management personnel must procure their Related Persons' compliance with clearance and notification obligations, and the short-term trading ban extends to them.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Subset of key management personnel with an additional duty to complete (or assist the company secretary to complete) an ASX Appendix 3X, 3Y or 3Z within three business days of appointment, a change of interest, or resignation.

definitions.hedging_definition: products which operate to limit economic risk in securities holdings in LIN

windows.start_anchor: 1 week before each date on which LIN gives its quarterly, half yearly or annual report to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: one business day after that date

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Additional periods imposed by the entity as soon as senior management is aware of a matter considered to be price sensitive (or which the Chairman or the MD deem to be price sensitive) form part of the 'Prohibited Period'. Confidentiality of these additional periods, or of refusal reasons, is not addressed.

rules.detail: Only permitted where LIN is not the counterparty (i.e. a third party such as a bank), the securities are fully vested, the derivative matures outside a Prohibited Period, it is used for the narrow protective purpose in the fourth criterion, and it complies with all applicable laws; the section 11 notification rules (two days' advance notice, post-trade confirmation) apply.
rules.evidence: Key management personnel may only enter into transactions involving derivatives ... in respect of LIN securities ... if the following criteria are satisfied: the relevant securities are fully vested; the Derivative has a maturity date that falls outside a Prohibited Period; LIN is not a counterparty to the Derivative; the Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by LIN or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable; and the Derivative transaction complies with all applicable laws.

rules.detail: The section 10 criteria require the underlying securities to be 'fully vested'; a derivative over unvested or holding-locked securities does not satisfy that precondition.
rules.evidence: the relevant securities are fully vested

rules.detail: No clearance, notification or derivative-specific regime applies to Applicable Persons who are not key management personnel; a derivative over LIN securities is simply a 'security' under the general definition, so only the general Inside Information dealing prohibition applies.
rules.evidence: securities include shares, derivatives and other financial products that can be traded on a financial market including financial products issued or created over LIN securities by third parties

rules.detail: A hedge ('product which operates to limit economic risk') is only permitted as a Derivative meeting the section 10 criteria, and specifically only where used to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan for option exercise price, or to protect against tax liabilities — not for general liquidity or diversification purposes.
rules.evidence: products which operate to limit economic risk in securities holdings in LIN ... the Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by LIN or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable

rules.detail: Same fully-vested precondition as derivatives generally bars hedging of unvested or holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: the relevant securities are fully vested

rules.detail: General purpose statement expressed to apply to all Applicable Persons, though the operative rule in section 6 narrows the substantive prohibition to key management personnel and their Related Persons.

rules.detail: Purchase and sale of the same securities within three months is prohibited at all times; the Board may exempt in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order).

clearance.approver: Board (prior written clearance to deal during a Prohibited Period, exceptional circumstances only); company secretary receives standing two-day advance notice of all intended dealings at any time
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two days of the dealing (confirmation of occurrence and price per security)
clearance.evidence: key management personnel are required to notify LIN of all intended dealings in LIN securities ... two days before such intended dealings ... Following completion of the proposed dealing, the relevant member of key management personnel must provide confirmation to the company secretary that the dealing has occurred, and details of the price per security, within two days of the dealing. The Board may, in exceptional circumstances only, give prior written clearance to any member of key management personnel or their Related Persons to deal in LIN securities during a Prohibited Period.

exemption_authority: The Board may, in exceptional circumstances only (severe financial hardship or court order), give prior written clearance to deal during a Prohibited Period (section 8), and may on application exempt a key management personnel or Related Person from the short-term trading prohibition in exceptional circumstances (section 6).

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by LIN or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar sought for general liquidity or diversification would not literally satisfy this narrow purpose test; the structure would need to be framed (and evidenced) as protecting collateral value for an exercise-price loan or a tax liability to fit within the permitted use.

bespoke_clauses.clause: LIN is not a counterparty to the Derivative
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This condition expressly contemplates (and requires) a third-party counterparty such as a bank, which is exactly the structure of an OTC funded collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: disposing of securities: ... as a result of a secured lender exercising their right under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the operation of this policy]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default of the secured loan is entirely excluded from the Prohibited Period and clearance requirements, removing the main practical obstacle other companies' policies impose on lender enforcement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Within ten days of a key management personnel or a Related Person entering into a margin lending arrangement involving LIN securities, the relevant key management personnel must provide the company secretary with the following information: the number of LIN securities that are subject to such arrangement; the trigger events for disposal of such securities; and any other information that may be relevant to LIN's continuous disclosure obligations, including the ability ... to meet any margin call.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: No Board pre-approval is required to grant security over the shares for financing (only for dealing that must occur during a Prohibited Period); a post-entry disclosure regime is the only gate, which is materially easier to satisfy than an outright ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: purpose statement vs operative rule mismatch
bespoke_clauses.clause: never engage in short term trading of LIN securities [section 1, applying to all Applicable Persons] versus key management personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from short-term trading at all times [section 6]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Worth confirming with the company secretary whether the short-term trading ban is intended to bind non-KMP Applicable Persons, since the only substantive, defined prohibition (three-month rule) is scoped to key management personnel.

summary: A funded collar with a bank is workable for key management personnel under this policy, though only within a narrow purpose gate. Section 10 permits KMP to enter derivative transactions with a third party (LIN itself cannot be the counterparty) over fully vested LIN securities, provided the derivative matures outside a Prohibited Period and is used specifically to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan for option exercise price or against tax liabilities; a collar sought for general liquidity or diversification would need to be framed to fit that purpose. Margin lending or other secured financing using LIN securities as collateral is separately and expressly permitted for KMP (section 9), subject only to ensuring the loan terms cannot force a trade during a Prohibited Period and to a ten-day post-entry disclosure to the company secretary (security numbers, disposal triggers, margin-call capacity); critically, a secured lender's forced sale on enforcement is expressly excluded from the policy altogether. All KMP dealings otherwise require two days' advance notice to the company secretary and post-trade confirmation within two days, and any dealing occurring inside a Prohibited Period needs the Board's prior written clearance, granted only in exceptional circumstances such as severe hardship or a court order.
